title: Graphs: Global Graphs and Straight-Line Graphs
seo_title: Grade 8 Graphs Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Analyse and interpret global graphs of problem situations, with special focus on trends and features: linear or non-linear, constant, increasing or decreasing, maximum or minimum, discrete or continuous; draw global graphs from given descriptions; use tables of ordered pairs to plot points and draw graphs on the Cartesian plane.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 8 graphs worksheets: global graphs, distance-time graphs, gradient, y-intercept and straight-line equations. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: y = mx + c: m is the gradient, c the y-intercept.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the axes and the scale first.
  • A global graph shows trends: increasing, decreasing, constant, maximum and minimum.
  • In y = mx + c, m is the gradient (steepness) and c is the y-intercept.
  • Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x.

Examples

Example

A line through (0; 2) and (3; 8)

gradient (8 − 2) ÷ 3 = 2

y-intercept 2

Answer: y = 2x + 2

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong axisRead the labels first.
m or c?c is where the line crosses the y-axis.
Upside downChange in y over change in x.
